newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY LEAGUE-Ridge expects Kiwis to be tested tonight.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY LEAGUE-Ridge expects Kiwis to be tested tonight.

text.p: New Zealand rugby league captain Matthew Ridge says he expects the Kiwis to be put through a sterner test of their character in tonight's first test against the Great Britain Lions at Auckland's Ericsson Stadium.
After outclassing Papua New Guinea in two recent tests, Ridge said the Kiwis were still to be tried, NZPA reports.
He should find out tonight just good his Kiwi outfit is.
"We haven't been tested yet, there is good team spirit and we've come together well but we still haven't really been put under pressure," Ridge said.
"Papua New Guinea, and no disrespect to them, didn't test us at all and I'm sure Great Britain will be a thousand times improvement on them."
Ridge said the Kiwis are bracing themselves for a torrid series and that was evident from the tension that was starting to creep into the Kiwis' camp yesterday for the first time this month.
"This is going to be a whole different ball game, the Poms are obviously a class side," Ridge, who is also the 1997 Auckland Warriors captain, said.
He said despite the Kiwis' heavy favouritism, nothing could be taken for granted.
"We're not thinking about winning the series three-nil, for a start we'd just like to win the series.
"Three-nil would be a huge bonus, but we know these guys are going to put up a helluva fight and it really is going to be anyone's ball game."
Like Ridge, Lions' captain Andy Farrell declared his team ready to rip into tonight's series' opener.

"I'm very happy with the way we've prepared. After last Thursday's performance (22-22 draw with the Lion Red 13) I wasn't very happy and we've had a bit of a kick up the backside since then," Farrell said.
"Everybody realised we had to get down to some hard work after that and hopefully we've done the work now."
Farrell said while the test team had only one training run for the first test, they had spent four weeks together and that meant they should be used to playing with each other.
"The lads have got to know each other's game now, we know this test is going to be a hard match and everyone is going to have to play for one another," he said.
"One of our big strengths is team spirit. We've got a lot of young players who want to play for one another and if we can click I'm sure the Kiwis will be in for a hard game."
Farrell is expecting a stormy first quarter against the big New Zealand pack.
"It could be quite fierce, we watched them against PNG and the forwards did a great job and their backs finished off the tries well.
"We've been working hard all week and hopefully we can contain them."
Australian referee Bill Harrigan, regarded as one of the best in the world, comes out of enforced exile since switching to Super League to control the first test.

NEW ZEALAND: Matthew Ridge (captain), Sean Hoppe, Richard Blackmore, John Timu, Richard Barnett, Gene Ngamu, Stacey Jones, Grant Young, Syd Eru, Quentin Pongia, Steve Kearney, Tony Iro, Tyran Smith. Replacements: Ruben Wiki, Joe Vagana, Marc Ellis, Logan Swann.

Great Britain: Stuart Spruce, Alan Hunte, Kris Radlinski, Daryl Powell, Anthony Sullivan, Iestyn Harris, Bobbie Goulding, Paul Broadbent, Keiron Cunningham, Terry O'Connor, Denis Betts, Paul Sculthorpe, Andy Farrell (captain). Replacements to be named. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
